context.note: Items marked merged are in the master branch only. They are not in a release until a release containing them is published.

status_scale.discussion: talked about on a list or forum, no concrete proposal
status_scale.proposal: written proposal (BIP draft, design doc, PR description) not yet merged
status_scale.merged: merged into a project's main branch, not yet released
status_scale.released: shipped in a tagged release of that software
status_scale.documentation: specification or documentation change only; no software behavior changes

items.title: Peers are no longer disconnected for a missed ping while they are sending us blocks
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core stops enforcing the 20-minute ping timeout against a peer while blocks are being downloaded from that peer.
items.why_it_matters: During initial block download on a slow link, a peer busy serving our block requests could miss the ping deadline and be dropped although it was not at fault. This avoids needless disconnects for low-bandwidth nodes.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. No consensus or policy change.

items.title: Private transaction broadcast now always completes all three initial connections
items.what_happened: When a node initiates a private broadcast of a transaction, it now completes all three initial broadcast connections instead of stopping early when the transaction comes back or conflicts.
items.why_it_matters: Stopping early could leak timing information that helps link a transaction to its origin. The PR addresses theoretical timing attacks raised in earlier review of the private-broadcast work.
affects: users who broadcast transactions privately through Bitcoin Core
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. Check release notes for when private broadcast and this fix ship.
items.uncertainty: The attacks addressed are described as theoretical in the PR.

items.title: Wallets track client versions and features for future upgrades
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core separates its recorded wallet-client version from the node version and records client feature flags, including those of the last client to decrypt the wallet.
items.why_it_matters: Groundwork for future automatic wallet upgrades: if a wallet is upgraded, opened in an older version, then opened in a newer one again, the newer client can detect this and redo the upgrade instead of leaving mixed upgraded and non-upgraded data.
affects: wallet users who switch between Bitcoin Core versions
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. Prepares for future automatic upgrades rather than introducing one.
items.uncertainty: The PR describes downgrade detection back to v24.0; later upgrade features still need implementation.

items.title: PSBT type registry adds the missing PSBT_IN_P2C_TWEAK (0x19) entry
items.what_happened: The BIP-174 PSBT field registry now lists input key type 0x19, PSBT_IN_P2C_TWEAK, defined in BIP-372 (pay-to-contract tweak fields). It had been left out when the tables moved into the registry.
items.why_it_matters: The registry exists so new BIPs do not reuse a key type that is already taken. A missing row risks a collision in a future proposal.
items.not_yet: Documentation fix only; no change to consensus, node software or existing PSBT behavior.

items.title: Postgres migration connections are closed to allow startup with small pools
items.what_happened: LND gives migration drivers separate database handles and closes each driver after use.
items.why_it_matters: Fresh databases previously retained 19 migration connections, preventing startup with a configured maximum below 20.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: Database lifecycle fix, not a Lightning protocol change.

items.title: Gossip CPU throttling no longer charges unrelated peer messages
items.what_happened: Core Lightning charges the gossip CPU budget only for incoming gossip queries and active replies.
items.why_it_matters: Ordinary traffic could exhaust small per-peer budgets and delay channel messages on busy nodes. Query-flood protection remains.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: The budget is still split evenly across peers.

items.title: Elements challenge bounds are checked before hashing
items.what_happened: Core Lightning checks challenge bytes before hashing Elements headers and safely handles failed parsing.
items.why_it_matters: Malformed backend blocks could trigger an out-of-bounds read or assertion failure.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: Requires malformed data from an Elements backend, not direct peer delivery.

items.title: macOS channel opening avoids a signer socket handoff race
items.what_happened: The signer retains a passed client socket until the next lightningd request confirms the handoff.
items.why_it_matters: Closing the sender copy too early could cause channeld to read EOF and exit, leaving channel opening stuck.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: The reported failure is macOS-specific and appears under load.

items.title: Truncated backend blocks are rejected without crashing
items.what_happened: Core Lightning checks transaction parsing before dereferencing the result and fixes a failed-parse memory leak.
items.why_it_matters: A block truncated inside a transaction could otherwise crash lightningd rather than be rejected.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: Requires a backend supplying malformed blocks, not direct Lightning peer delivery.

items.title: CCAN update brings I/O and file-descriptor reliability fixes
items.what_happened: Core Lightning updates CCAN with fixes including I/O busy-spinning, nonblocking listeners, subprocess handling, descriptor leaks and path simplification.
items.why_it_matters: Several fixes can affect connection and subprocess behavior, beyond tests or library cleanup.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: The PR distinguishes potentially relevant fixes from many upstream changes unused by CLN; no general exploit claim is established.

items.title: Replacement closing scripts are validated throughout shutdown
items.what_happened: Eclair validates changed peer closing scripts in later shutdown and closing messages, ignoring invalid replacements and warning.
items.why_it_matters: A peer could otherwise bypass upfront shutdown-script constraints or inflate closing fees using a large replacement script.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: Implementation enforcement of existing BOLT 2 requirements, not a new protocol rule.

items.title: Previously accepted closing scripts survive feature renegotiation
items.what_happened: Eclair skips redundant checks for unchanged accepted closing scripts, preserving fresh nonce processing after reconnection.
items.why_it_matters: Revalidating against renegotiated features could reject an unchanged script and leave cooperative closing stuck with a stale nonce.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: Initially merged into remote-closing-script; its merge commit is included in master PR #3387, merged October 6.

items.title: Interactive funding is hardened against a dishonest bitcoind
items.what_happened: Eclair verifies actual fees from spent outputs when a fee budget applies and checks reconstructed funding contributions and change positions.
items.why_it_matters: In Eclair signer mode, a compromised backend without signing keys could manipulate dual-funding or splicing to waste funds on excessive mining fees.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: Hardens specific funding paths, not every interaction with a compromised backend.

items.title: Invalid seed lengths now prevent startup
items.what_happened: Eclair requires 32-byte seeds or its legacy 33-byte format ending in 0x01, retaining legacy bytes unchanged.
items.why_it_matters: A crash before seed writing could leave an empty file; restarting previously derived node and channel keys from that empty input.
items.not_yet: In the main development branch only; not in a release. Limited to this implementation.
items.uncertainty: Rejects malformed files but does not recover a lost seed.
